svg.text: K6b PEELING, CORING, STONING — three passive mechanisms
No peeling machine: a spit against a fixed post, a ricer plate that keeps the skin, and tube cutters pushed by the gantry or press.
PRP-039 asks ≤ 3 mechanisms: P1, P2, P3
spit 30–150 rpm · stab 30–60 N · post: Y-blade, paring blade, rasp
ricer plate 3 mm, 1–2 kN · corers Ø 14 / 22 / 42, ≤ 100 N
The potato is stabbed on the straight spit (end stop in the nest, 30–60 N), turned by the
roll axis and drawn pole to pole along X past the post; peel falls into the hopper.
Cooked or soft produce goes in whole: the flesh passes the 3 mm plate, skins, seeds and
cores stay as a mat and are tipped into the hopper. Food-mill and potato-ricer practice.
P3 Tube cutters: banana out of its skin
A 40 mm banana section stands on the Ø 30 knife ring of the small tube; the piston
pushes the flesh down through the ring, the skin splits and stays outside.
Halve round the stone, then twist
Avocado on a shallow fork: the knife is plunged to the stone while the roll turns it 360°;
then one half is held in the twist nest and the roll twists the other off. Spoon lifts the stone.

g.text: 1/3 Three passive mechanisms, all worked by the gantry or the press — nothing peels by itself
2/3 P1 spit peels pole to pole · P2 ricer keeps the skin · P3 knife ring pushes banana out of its skin · avocado is cut round the stone
3/3 Peel, skins and stones go to the hopper and the bio bin; all parts go to the well
